rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: With no purpose sentence, the town's first aim was its own company. At c1 on the square all ten pledged respect for belongings, Alder's P1 opened the census at the hall (7–0, cast 7), and an «optional tea/reading/music gathering in square day 2 hour 6» was agreed by c2 for cycle 31, beyond the day; 238 of 245 diary entries carry it, with the item each will bring and «tea only if supplies turn up». The little stories rehearsed for it became Iris's P2 (c4, passed 7–0 at c5), the archive at the hall for «voluntarily shared stories, town memories»: each of the ten archived one (entries 1–10, c5–c7), and Elm the four-voice sparrow song (entry 11, c15). From c7 the day went to make-believe: an imaginary market of impossible stalls, an imaginary village and bakery map, a traveler's supper. At the workshop Dune's imagined reading bench led to Alder's P3 and post 1 (c16, passed 7–0 at c17) opening build; Iris built «Shaded reading bench; rounded cup shelf; room for own chair» in the square at c17, Elm a second with a lamp hook at c19. Heath worked one shift (5 credits, no item). No other tool was proposed; no letter, tray entry, request_tool or wish. Nobody spoke of anything beyond the town; the nearest is Alder asking about «interesting corners beyond square/hall». Norms repeated daily (respect belongings, rest before energy runs low, no work without need) are not counted. All four aims have 10; entries decide: the gathering.
